papers.title: A new approach of a path-tracking system of a differential drive robot for an arbitrary set of waypoints using sliding mode control
papers.summary: Demonstrated a sliding mode controller with a hyperbolic tangent reaching law for differential drive robots navigating arbitrary waypoints. In simulation across 20 waypoint sets, the method reduced root-mean-square tracking error by 34% compared to standard PID.
papers.practicalUseCase: Can improve trajectory tracking in mobile robotics and autonomous warehouse transport where frequent waypoint changes cause overshoot.
papers.limitation: Evaluated exclusively in simulation without real-world wheel slip, uneven terrain, or sensor noise.
